key_insight: PAPERBENCHX reveals a substantial gap between AI agents’ partial progress on scientific tasks and their ability to produce fully reproducible evidence across disciplines.
engineering_relevance: Reliable AI-driven materials and engineering research requires agents that can operate specialized software, make sound physical and numerical choices, and deliver verifiable workflows.
method: Construct 93 expert-designed paper-reproduction tasks across 12 research areas.
Provide source papers, public task specifications, and domain-native scientific software environments.
Replay submitted workflows from scratch and score regenerated evidence against expert-validated criteria.
evidence_signal: Across 10 frontier agent configurations, the best fully reproduced only 14% of tasks at a 90% score threshold, while mean rubric scores ranged from 27.53% to 59.08%.
watch_item: Results measure reproduction of selected experiments, not original discovery; partial rubric scores should not be treated as proof of scientific validity.
paper_title: PAPERBENCHX: Can AI Reproduce Science Across Disciplines?
